section: common mistakes and misconceptions
text: Its hidden state is never trained to reproduce the observation or to match the true state. "MCTS needs random rollouts." Classic MCTS and AlphaGo used them; AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero and MuZero score each new leaf with a value network and do no rollouts at all. "Planning is free experience." It is free of real experience, not of computation: n = 50 Dyna does 50 updates per real step, AlphaGo Zero spent about 0.4 s and 1,600 network evaluations per move, AlphaZero used 5,000 TPUs to generate its games. "A model with lower one-step error will plan better." Not necessarily: errors compound over long rollouts and planners exploit them, and one-step likelihood "is not always correlated with control performance" (objective mismatch).
